summary: Describes how to build point-to-multipoint label switched paths that span several routing areas. The path is split into segments inside each area, and BGP is used to stitch the segments together between areas. This keeps the per-area routing protocols independent while still delivering multicast-style traffic across a large network.

plainLanguage.summary: One TV broadcast has to reach many towns. Each town gets its own local cable, and a coordinator connects the local cables to one another so the show gets everywhere without any town needing a map of all the others.

questions: what is an inter-area p2mp lsp
how does mpls multicast work across ospf areas
what is the inter-area p2mp segmented next-hop extended community
subtitle: How to carry one-to-many MPLS traffic across several routing areas by cutting the path into per-area pieces glued together with BGP.

tldr.problem: When thousands of provider edge routers sit in different IGP areas, a single point-to-multipoint path across all of them is hard to build and keep track of.
tldr.mechanism: The service LSP is split into an ingress area segment, a backbone area segment and egress area segments. BGP Leaf A-D routes and a new extended community stitch the segments together at the area border routers.
tldr.outcome: Area border routers only do MPLS switching, and each area keeps its own tunnels. RFC 7524 is a Proposed Standard, and RFC 8534 updates it.

today: RFC 7524 is a Proposed Standard, published in May 2015, and it is updated by RFC 8534. The RFC text does not describe any deployments.

sections.title: Why Segment a Multicast Path
sections.content:
RFC 7524 describes how to build inter-area point-to-multipoint (P2MP) segmented service LSPs. The idea is to partition such an LSP into intra-area segments and to use BGP as the inter-area routing and label distribution protocol.

The primary use case is a network where Provider Edge (PE) routers are in different areas of the same Autonomous System and thousands or more of them need P2MP connectivity. The RFC gives the example of MPLS being pushed further to the metro edge with the metros in different IGP areas, and says the document describes the multicast procedures for seamless MPLS.

The services that use these LSPs can be BGP Multicast VPN, VPLS multicast, or global table multicast over MPLS. The document complements RFC 6514 and RFC 7117, which already cover segmented inter-AS P2MP service LSPs.
sections.plainLanguage: A very big network is split into neighbourhoods. Instead of one giant delivery route covering everything, each neighbourhood gets its own small route, and the routes are joined at the borders.

sections.title: Three Segments and Their Roots
sections.content:
Within an AS, a P2MP service LSP is partitioned into three segments: the ingress area segment, the backbone area segment and the egress area segment. Each is carried over an intra-area P2MP LSP or built with ingress replication.

  • The ingress area segment is rooted at a PE (or an ASBR). Its leaves are other PEs, ASBRs and ABRs in the same area.
  • The backbone area segment is rooted at the ingress ABR. Its leaves are the ABRs that connect to the egress areas.
  • The egress area segment is rooted at an egress ABR and has the leaf PEs of that area as its leaves.

There may be more than one backbone segment and more than one egress segment for the same service LSP. ABRs acting as route reflectors set the BGP Next Hop to themselves (next-hop-self) when reflecting routes from non-backbone areas into the backbone, and SHOULD NOT change it (next-hop-unchanged) in the other direction, as in seamless MPLS.

When several segments share one intra-area P2MP LSP, MPLS P2MP LSP hierarchy with upstream-assigned labels is used. A one-to-one mapping uses an Implicit NULL label.
sections.plainLanguage: The trip has three legs: the starting town, the highway in the middle, and the destination towns. Each leg has its own driver, and the border stations hand the cargo from one leg to the next.

sections.title: Finding the Tree and Joining It with BGP
sections.content:
Egress PEs first learn the P2MP FEC (the identity of the tree) from configuration or application-specific routes: MVPN I-PMSI or S-PMSI A-D routes, VPLS A-D routes, or, for global table multicast, IGMP or PIM messages that give an (S/*,G).

Routes that should be segmented carry the new Inter-Area P2MP Segmented Next-Hop Extended Community. Its Global Administrator field is the IP address of the PE, ABR or ASBR that advertises the route, and its Local Administrator field MUST be 0. Each ABR sets it to its own address when it re-advertises the route. ABRs MUST NOT change the BGP Next Hop of these routes.

Each egress PE works out its upstream node (an egress ABR, an ingress ABR or the ingress PE, depending on where it sits) and MUST originate a Leaf A-D route if the route requires leaf information. The route carries an IP-based Route Target holding the upstream node's address, so only that node imports it. The egress ABR then originates its own Leaf A-D route toward the upstream node in the backbone, and the ingress ABR does the same toward the ingress area, until the root PE has the leaves it needs.
sections.plainLanguage: Each receiver raises its hand and tells the next station up the line, "send it to me." That station raises its own hand to the next station, and so on up to the sender.

sections.title: Global Table Multicast and PIM Options
sections.content:
For global table multicast, the Leaf A-D route uses a Route Key that holds an RD, the multicast source (or RP), the multicast group and the ingress PE's address. The RD is set to 0 for (S,G) state and all ones for (*,G) state. A router tells these apart from MVPN and VPLS Leaf A-D routes by the third octet of the MCAST-VPN NLRI: 0x01, 0x02 or 0x03 means MVPN or VPLS, while 0x00 or 0xff means global table multicast.

The address family of the two address fields is taken from their length, 4 octets for IPv4 or 16 octets for IPv6, and not from the AFI. So an IPv4 network can carry IPv6 multicast service.

For PIM-SM in ASM mode there are two options. Option 1 does not carry shared trees over the MPLS network, so (*,G) state is not propagated with Leaf A-D routes. Option 2 does carry shared trees and supports switching to source trees. Both use BGP Source Active A-D routes, which SHOULD carry the NO_EXPORT community, and Option 2 can prune sources off the shared tree after a configurable timer.
sections.plainLanguage: For regular TV channels with no special club, the network watches which channels people ask for and sets up the delivery for just those channels.

sections.title: Intra-Area Tunnels and the Data Plane
sections.content:
Inside each area, a segment can ride in a P2MP RSVP-TE LSP, a P2MP LDP LSP, or use ingress replication. With ingress replication the sender copies each packet to every leaf over P2P RSVP-TE or MP2P LDP LSPs, with the bottom label being a distinct downstream-assigned label from the leaf.

On the data plane, ABRs and transit routers perform only MPLS switching. An ABR pops the incoming label stack and pushes the stack of the outgoing P2MP LSP, first pushing the upstream-assigned label if the mapping is many-to-one. For global table multicast with many-to-one mapping, packets from an unexpected upstream node MUST be dropped, so the intra-area P2MP LSP MUST be signaled with no Penultimate Hop Popping.

If the root PE needs the same tunnel type in the ingress and egress areas while the backbone uses another, the ingress ABR saves the original PMSI Tunnel attribute in an ATTR_SET attribute and the egress ABR restores the tunnel type from it.
sections.plainLanguage: Each neighbourhood can use a single bus that stops at every house, or a delivery person who makes one copy of the package per house. Either way, the border station just moves the package from one vehicle to the next.

sections.title: Optional Transport LSPs
sections.content:
An optional section lets a root PE bundle several inter-area service LSPs into one inter-area P2MP transport LSP and segment that instead. It defines a new PMSI tunnel type, "Transport Tunnel", with value 8. Its identifier is the pair of the Source PE Address and a Local Number of the same length.

The RFC discusses the trade-off. Bundling can reduce the state ABRs hold, but only if one transport LSP carries more than one service LSP. It also concentrates leaf tracking on the ingress PE and can waste bandwidth, because traffic reaches PEs that have no receivers. The RFC's worked example has PE1 send two streams that would then also reach PE5 or PE2 needlessly.
sections.plainLanguage: You can put several parcels in one big truck to keep the border station simple. But then the truck may visit houses that did not order every parcel.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA has assigned 0x12 in the Transitive IPv4-Address-Specific Extended Community Sub-Types registry and 0x0012 in the IPv6 registry for the new extended community. It assigned 0x08 for the "Transport Tunnel" PMSI tunnel type, and the Route Distinguisher type value 65535 for use only in certain Leaf A-D routes.

The security section is short. The procedures face threats similar to any MPLS deployment, and it recommends the baseline measures in the security framework for MPLS and GMPLS networks (RFC 5920), the mLDP specification (RFC 6388) and the P2MP RSVP-TE specification (RFC 3209). The security considerations of RFC 6513 also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: The new system gets the same safety rules as other delivery networks of this kind, plus a few new official numbers so everyone uses the same names.
